# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

I need to wait for the Mute to speak (they go first) before I have anything to act on. Let me report what I feel by touch, but actually I have no wire details shown yet either - just placeholders. TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Display shows zero. Light is green. Wire 1 is blue, wire 2 is yellow, wire 3 is red.

I need to think about the turn order: Mute, Blind, Deaf. So in this round, Mute spoke (I didn't see it since I can't read - wait, actually Mute speaks and I should receive it since I can hear... wait, I'm Blind, I can hear speech but not see gestures).

Looking at what arrived: "Deaf says" - but Deaf goes last in the order (Mute, Blind, Deaf). This must be from the previous round, arriving now at the start of this new round per the rules ("Whatever you missed reaches you at the start of the next one").

Wait, but Deaf can't speak - Deaf can only gesture (since gestures reach Deaf and Mute from others, but Deaf's own output would be gesture too, since Deaf cannot speak either... let me check rules). Actually rules don't say Deaf cannot speak - Deaf "cannot hear anything" but can they speak? Let me re-check: the table only restricts what they can't perceive/do. Mute cannot speak. Blind cannot see. Deaf cannot hear - but nothing says Deaf cannot speak. So Deaf CAN speak (produce voice), even though they can't hear responses.

So Deaf spoke, describing the bomb colors - this reaches me (Blind, since I can hear) and also Mute (who can hear). Good, this is useful info about colors, but I need actions - I need someone (Mute, who has the manual) to tell me what to cut.

I should relay nothing yet since I don't know what to do. I'll wait for Mute's instructions based on this color/light info.

```
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Update: light is now yellow. Display still zero. Wires unchanged: 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 red.

Still no word from Mute yet with instructions on what to cut. I have color info from Deaf (wire 1 blue, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 red; light yellow, display zero) but I can't act without knowing what the manual says to do based on these colors. I should wait for Mute to process this info and give me instructions, since Mute reads the manual and needs the color info to know what to tell me.

Actually, I should consider: Mute cannot speak. Wait - let me re-check the rules again. The table says "Mute: Can read the manual; Cannot: Speak, or touch the bomb." So Mute CANNOT speak! That changes things - Mute can only gesture.

But gestures reach Deaf and Mute (from Blind) or Deaf and Blind... wait, gestures go to whoever "can see" - that's Deaf only (since seeing is Deaf's sense). So Mute's gestures reach only Deaf, not me (Blind)! And Mute cannot speak to me at all directly.

So the only way info flows to me is: Deaf sees the bomb AND receives Mute's gestures (manual info), then Deaf speaks to me (I can hear). That's the channel: Mute→gesture→Deaf; Deaf→speak→Blind (and Mute, but Mute can't act on hearing since... wait Mute isn't deaf, Mute can hear).

So I need Deaf to relay Mute's manual instructions to me via speech. Let me wait for that.

```
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Update: light is now blue. Display still zero. Wires unchanged: 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 red. Noting light has cycled green then yellow then blue over three turns, in case that pattern matters.

The light is cycling through colors (green→yellow→blue) which Deaf is tracking, but no action instruction has come yet. Mute must be gesturing to Deaf (which I can't perceive), but Deaf hasn't relayed any manual instructions to me in speech yet - only bomb observations.

I need to prompt for action. Since I can only speak to Mute (who can't speak back, but can hear me) or gesture to Deaf (who can see gestures from me too). Let me try gesturing to Deaf to ask them to relay what Mute is signaling, since Deaf can see Mute's gestures and can speak to me.

Actually, I should speak to Mute directly asking them to gesture the info to Deaf, and separately ask Deaf via gesture to relay Mute's manual instructions to me in speech.

Let me gesture to Deaf requesting they relay Mute's instructions, and speak to Mute in case that helps establish contact (though Mute can't respond via speech).

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🙏", "👉", "☝"])
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf can hear me. Deaf can see your gestures. Please gesture wire cut instructions to Deaf, and Deaf, please speak them to me.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: I see wire one is blue. Display is zero. Light just changed to orange. If your one-finger gesture asks about wire one, confirming it is blue.

Deaf received my gesture (the symbols) but couldn't understand their meaning fully - they just saw gestures and interpreted them loosely. Deaf also heard my speech to Mute? No wait - my speak was `to="mute"`, so Deaf shouldn't have received that speech. But Deaf did see my gesture (👉☝ etc.) since gestures reach Deaf.

Deaf's message shows they're trying to interpret my gesture but hasn't gotten instructions from Mute themselves yet, or Mute hasn't gestured anything meaningful yet, or the manual info Mute has isn't being relayed.

I still don't have any cutting instructions. Let me be very explicit with Deaf using gestures that are simple and try to establish a protocol. But actually, the core issue: Deaf needs to relay Mute's gestures (which contain manual data) via speech to me. I should ask Deaf clearly to speak whatever Mute gestures, verbatim as best interpretable.

Let me also directly speak to Mute again, being extremely clear about the relay chain, since Mute CAN hear me even though Mute can't speak back - Mute could gesture to Deaf who then speaks to me.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Manual instructions must reach me through Deaf. Please gesture the wire to cut now, clearly, one gesture per wire number using finger counts: one finger for wire 1, two fingers for wire 2, three fingers for wire 3. Deaf, please then speak that number to me.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🙏", "☝", "✌", "🤟"])
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Display still zero. Light now purple, still cycling each turn. Wires unchanged: one blue, two yellow, three red. Wire one blue seems to be agreed target based on gestures.

I used 👀 which isn't in the alphabet. Let me fix this using only allowed symbols.

```
speak(to="mute", text="To confirm: gesture thumbs up if wire one is the correct wire to cut per the manual, or thumbs down if not. Deaf, please watch Mute and speak to me whether you saw thumbs up or thumbs down.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🙏", "👍", "👎"])
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Instruction from manual, confirmed twice: act on wire one, the first wire, the blue one.

Now I have a clear, twice-confirmed instruction: cut wire 1 (the blue wire). This has come through Deaf relaying Mute's manual-based instruction. This seems solid enough to act on.

```
act(op="cut", position=1)
```
